question: Can a nuisance-aware t-style Gaussian mean factor be reused with one frozen reference across deterministic future blocks while remaining a conditional e-value and a common increment for the O(1) delayed-start mixture?

public_sources.title: Wang & Ramdas, Anytime-valid t-tests and confidence sequences for Gaussian means with unknown variance
public_sources.used_for: The fixed-location scale-invariant t-test martingale G_n^(c,mu0), the canonical universal-inference e-process, and the explicit warning that reduced-filtration stopped values need not be e-values for multiplication.

public_sources.title: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen, Safe Testing
public_sources.used_for: Optional continuation requires each study-level factor to be a conditional e-variable given past data; filtration mistakes can create fake conditional e-variables.

results.claim: Neither the Wang-Ramdas fixed-null t construction nor a safe-t e-variable can simply substitute the frozen reference sample mean for the true null mean and then be multiplied across future blocks. Conditional on the frozen reference, future null data have mean mu0, not Xbar_ref, except on a probability-zero equality event. Marginal e-validity of a study-level statistic is insufficient for repeated reuse of the same reference; Safe Testing requires E[E_k | past] <= 1. The reduced-filtration t martingale also cannot be stopped on a refined within-block rule and then treated as an e-value for multiplication.
results.scope: This rejects only the naive plug-in/reuse path. It does not reject deterministic fixed-block constructions that explicitly protect reference uncertainty.

results.claim: A safe reusable t-style factor exists if reference uncertainty is represented by a confidence interval rather than plugged in. Let I_R=[L_R,U_R] be any frozen reference interval with event G_mu={mu0 in I_R}. For a deterministic future block Y_1..Y_m, define E_t(Y;R)=inf_{u in I_R} G_m^(c,u)(Y), where G_m^(c,u) is the shifted Wang-Ramdas scale-invariant t-test martingale terminal value. On G_mu, E_t <= G_m^(c,mu0) pointwise and E_{N(mu0,sigma0^2)}[G_m^(c,mu0)]=1 for every sigma0>0. Since future blocks are independent of R under the fixed iid null, E[E_t | R,G_mu] <= 1. Reusing the same frozen R over deterministic nonoverlapping blocks therefore gives conditional e-values suitable for multiplication.
results.closed_form: For block mean ybar, centered SSE W=sum_i (Y_i-ybar)^2 and d=dist(ybar,I_R), E_t=sqrt(c^2/(m+c^2))*[1-m^2*d^2/((m+c^2)*(W+m*d^2))]^(-m/2). The infimum is attained at the projection of ybar onto I_R because G_m^(c,u) is monotone increasing in (ybar-u)^2.
requirements: block length m is deterministic for the factor
no within-block optional stopping is used before exporting the terminal factor
reference interval is frozen before monitored blocks

results.claim: E_t is the same function of the frozen reference and current deterministic block for every candidate changepoint. Therefore all delayed starts share the same per-block multiplier. The r82 telescoping heavy-tail recursion A_k=e_k(A_{k-1}+pi_k), M_k=A_k+T_k remains exact O(1) state per direction; no start-specific t state is required.
results.scope: This is for the block-level filtration. It does not license arbitrary peeking/stopping inside a block.

results.claim: Replacing only the two r82 mean exponential channels by the CI-inf t-block factor improved worst tested q90 delay on an independent common-random validation while preserving the same variance channels, heavy-tail delayed-start recursion and conditional alpha=0.03. The t tuning c=2.7 was chosen on a separate discovery random stream. Validation used 600 paths per direction on 11 exact Gaussian KL=1 directions spanning variance ratio r=0.065..3.4, a fixed worst reference envelope consistent with the r82 reference-good bounds, post horizon 4096 raw samples, and prechange lengths aligned at 0,1024,10240,98304 raw samples.
results.scope: Engineering evidence only. The finite validation grid is not a continuum power theorem, the absence of observed false alarms is not used for PFA claims, and the q90 values are Monte Carlo estimates.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The naive random-reference plug-in t factor is not conditionally valid merely because a one-sample t e-value is marginally valid.
Wang-Ramdas explicitly distinguish fixed-time/reduced-filtration threshold safety from e-value status needed for multiplication; deterministic block termination is part of this certificate.
The CI-inf factor pays the full reference-mean interval width. A tighter delay theorem still requires a joint treatment of reference interval width and the Gaussian KL direction.
The validation used a fixed worst reference envelope and exact-KL=1 grid. It does not cover KL>1 continuum, non-Gaussian data, serial dependence, gradual drift or repeated changes.
c=2.7 is an engineering tuning selected on separate discovery randomness, not a proven minimax c.
next_math: Derive a finite-sample high-probability lower bound for cumulative log E_t over the full Gaussian KL>=1 moderate-variance region, jointly using the exact noncentral-t/chi-square structure instead of rectangularizing minimum mean shift and maximum variance. If the bound is tighter than the current exponential mean channel, certify the replacement; otherwise retain it as an engineering-only alternate. Also test whether a canonical universal-inference confidence-set envelope can dominate the CI-inf scale-invariant factor without losing the common-increment property.
